messages:
Tom (AE): Quick sync - Prospect BankX wants a Private/VPC POC. Requirements: preserve client source IP for fraud scoring, restrict outbound to a single /30 for compliance, and prefer no route-table surgery. Can we scope?
Sofia (Solutions): Two patterns: (A) Deploy our connector inside their VPC (customer-hosted) -> preserves source IP and supports BYOIP egress. (B) PrivateLink (Interface Endpoint) -> minimal routing changes, ENIs are created in their subnets. Tradeoff: PrivateLink + Redwood-managed egress will SNAT and lose original srcIP unless the connector runs in their account.
Jared (NetOps): If they insist on a single /30, we can reserve a tiny EIP pool for the POC and egress NAT from our side, but that removes srcIP. To preserve srcIP and still have predictable egress, they must host the connector and use their BYOIP or NAT gateway.
Leah (Security): TLS inspection note: if BankX terminates TLS at perimeter and strips SNI, hostname-based routing to our backend might fail. Options: 1) allow TLS passthrough for Redwood hostnames, 2) install our certs into their TLS inspection device, or 3) run connector in-VPC so traffic never leaves their inspection domain.
Tom (AE): Procurement asked for a one-paragraph network blurb to paste in the security questionnaire. Can someone draft a short, copy-paste answer?
Sofia (Solutions): Paste this (one para):
"Network Architecture (Private POC): Redwood supports two deployment options. Option 1 (recommended for source-IP preservation): customer deploys the Redwood connector into their VPC; application traffic is routed to the in-VPC connector and outbound control-plane traffic from the connector uses TLS (TCP/443). Option 2: AWS PrivateLink (Interface VPC Endpoint) which creates ENIs in customer subnets and avoids route-table edits; note that if Redwood manages outbound egress, connections may be SNATed to Redwood EIPs and original client source IPs will not be seen by the customer backend. Required firewall changes are minimal: open TLS (443) from connector to Redwood control-plane EIP ranges (provided during onboarding) and allow app->endpoint TLS if using PrivateLink. No public inbound exposure is required."
Jared (NetOps): Minimal SG snippet for their infra runbook (pasteable):
# Allow application subnet to reach interface endpoint ENIs
aws ec2 authorize-security-group-ingress --group-id sg-app --protocol tcp --port 443 --cidr 10.20.30.0/24
# Allow connector outbound to Redwood control-plane (example /30 we can reserve)
aws ec2 authorize-security-group-egress --group-id sg-connector --protocol tcp --port 443 --cidr 198.51.100.4/30
Jared (NetOps): MTU/truncation: if they use SD-WAN or IPsec with lower MTU, we see truncated payloads. Recommend they confirm path MTU; short-term fix is MSS clamping on the connector host: 
iptables -t mangle -A POSTROUTING -p tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN -j TCPMSS --clamp-mss-to-pmtu
Leah (Security): Compliance Q: Packet captures for audit — we need to document redaction and retention. If they host connector we can log locally and match their retention policies; if Redwood manages egress, provide SOC2 controls and agreed retention period. I can prepare a short appendix.
Tom (AE): Pricing/POC ask: how much delta vs Dedicated and any one-time fees? Keep it ballpark for procurement.
Sofia (Solutions): Ballpark: single-AZ customer-hosted POC = onboarding fee + platform license; expect ~1.2x hosted for small trials because of connector infra ops. If we manage connector + reserved /30 EIPs, add a monthly connector service fee. I'll follow up with a canned cost appendix.
ticket-bot: POC workspace created: redwood-poc-bankx-5861 (id poc-bx-5861). Link: https://internal.redwood/pocs/poc-bx-5861
Tom (AE): Great. Next actions: Leah will draft the packet-capture/retention appendix; Jared will confirm exact /30 EIP values and healthcheck TTL recommendations; Sofia will attach the cost appendix + simple two-box diagram (PrivateLink vs in-VPC) and I'll send the questionnaire text to BankX procurement.
Sofia (Solutions): I'll upload the diagram and cost appendix into the POC workspace in ~2 hours.
Jared (NetOps): I'll DM the /30 and suggested healthcheck 60s TTL within the hour.
Leah (Security): I'll prepare the retention blurb and include SOC2 references.
Tom (AE): Thanks all :thumbsup:
